1: David is old. His son Adonijah tries to take the throne. Nathan and Bathsheba remind David of his promise, and Solomon is anointed.
2: David tells Solomon to be strong and keep God's law, and dies. Solomon secures the kingdom against his rivals.
The kingdom depends on faithfulness to God.
3: God offers Solomon anything. He asks for an understanding heart to govern well. He proves it when two women claim the same baby.
Solomon asks for what helps him serve, and receives the rest besides.
4: A list of his officials. Judah and Israel live in peace, each under his vine and fig tree. Solomon's wisdom is famous.
A glimpse of the peace God intends.
5: Solomon arranges with King Hiram of Tyre for cedar wood and gathers workers.
A foreign king helps build God's house.
6: Solomon builds the Temple in seven years, with an inner sanctuary overlaid with gold for the ark.
God promises to dwell there if Solomon walks in his ways.
7: Solomon builds his own palace and has the bronze pillars, the great basin and the gold vessels made for the Temple.
Beauty and craftsmanship are offered to God.
8: The ark is brought in and the cloud of God's glory fills the house. Solomon prays that God will hear every prayer made toward this place, even a foreigner's.
"Heaven itself cannot contain you." The Temple is a house of prayer.
9: God appears again: if Solomon is faithful, his throne will stand; if Israel turns to other gods, the Temple will become ruins.
10: The queen comes with hard questions and is overwhelmed by Solomon's wisdom and wealth.
Jesus says that "something greater than Solomon is here".
11: Solomon marries many foreign wives and builds shrines for their gods. God announces that the kingdom will be torn in two. Solomon dies.
The wisest man is undone by a divided heart.
12: Rehoboam answers the people harshly, and ten tribes break away under Jeroboam, who sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan.
Arrogance divides the nation, and convenience creates false worship.
13: The man of God from Judah
A prophet condemns the altar at Bethel. He is then deceived into disobeying God's command and is killed by a lion.
God's word must be obeyed even against a persuasive voice.
14: The prophet Ahijah foretells the end of Jeroboam's house. In Judah, Rehoboam's people turn to idols, and Egypt plunders the Temple.
15: In Judah, Abijam is followed by Asa, who removes idols. In Israel, kings are murdered and replaced.
Each king is judged by one thing: whether he was faithful to God.
16: Coups follow one another in Israel. Omri builds Samaria. His son Ahab marries Jezebel and builds a temple of Baal.
Ahab does more evil than all before him.
17: Elijah announces a drought. Ravens feed him by a brook. Then a poor widow shares her last flour and oil, which never run out, and Elijah raises her son.
God provides day by day for those who trust him.
18: Elijah challenges 450 prophets of Baal. They cry out all day with no answer. Elijah prays, and fire falls on his drenched sacrifice. Rain returns.
"How long will you limp between two opinions?"
19: Threatened by Jezebel, Elijah flees and wants to die. An angel feeds him, and at Mount Horeb God comes not in wind, earthquake or fire but in a gentle whisper. Elijah calls Elisha.
God meets his exhausted prophet with food, rest and quiet.
20: God twice gives Ahab victory over the king of Syria. Ahab then spares him, and a prophet rebukes him.
God helps even Ahab, who still does not listen.
21: Naboth will not sell his family land. Jezebel has him falsely accused and stoned, and Ahab takes the vineyard. Elijah confronts him.
God defends the ordinary man against the powerful.
22: Four hundred prophets promise victory. Micaiah alone tells the truth. Ahab goes into battle disguised and is killed by a random arrow.
The truth is not decided by majority.
